result.title: SteerTrace: Tracing How Target Attacks Steer World Action Models
result.summary: World action models (WAMs) predict future videos and actions with one backbone, and their imagined future is often seen as a safety signal. We introduce SteerTrace, a targeted universal attack on WAMs that also traces its effect inside the model. One $\ell_\infty$-bounded (4/255) perturbation per model, shared across frames, tasks, and camera views, pushes the executed action toward an attacker-chosen target. On eight WAMs from four families (FastWAM, Faster-WAM, OpenWAM and LingBot-VA) on LIBERO and RoboTwin, it drives task success close to zero and moves the attacked action toward the target. Same-budget noise and BadWAM produce little action shift in the target direction. We use the signed targeted effect to measure how much of the effect each intervention removes or reproduces. Under the standard attack, restoring future tokens removes 61-94% of the targeted effect in the five models whose action experts attend to them. When the attack is constrained to keep the predicted future close to the clean prediction, the targeted effect can become more dependent on current-frame tokens. In three of these five models, restoring current-frame tokens removes 87-99% of the effect, compared with 9-15% for future tokens. In six models, restoring just 0.36% of the FFN neurons in layers 10-29 of the video expert removes 72-96% of the targeted effect. Residual directions 2-16 hold only 11-18% of the shift energy, yet removing them cancels most of the targeted effect.

AI.brief_summary: 提出 SteerTrace，一种针对世界动作模型的通用目标攻击：单个共享扰动即可把执行动作推向指定目标，并通过恢复未来 token、当前帧 token、少数 FFN 神经元和残差方向来测量各内部成分对攻击效应的贡献。
AI.relevance_reason: 其「有符号目标效应 + 逐层恢复内部状态」的因果归因流程，可能可供核查 LVR 中哪些 latent 或视觉证据承载答案相关贡献、贡献如何在 token 与神经元间分配；但研究对象是动作模型的对抗攻击，与多模态推理仅方法层面相关。
